notes: Phase 28 meets every acceptance criterion in code and tests: AIProvider abstraction with Anthropic/OpenAI behind a host-pinned guarded fetch, BYOK key encrypted as ai_provider_key with type-asserted settings and same-transaction replacement, a frozen 10-tool read-only registry with per-tool Zod schemas and the fixed JSON envelope, a capped agent loop with grounding/hallucination stripping, SSE ask API with 401/404/409/413/422/429, heartbeats, abort propagation and failed/aborted persistence, and the AI leak canary wired into security:scan-leaks. Verified by running typecheck, lint, boundaries, 256 unit tests, 32 integration tests (settings/tools/api) and the canary-ai suite on Ubuntu 24.04, all green. No scope creep. | findings: Non-blocking: apps/control-plane/src/ai/conversations/ask-service.ts hardcodes scope {kind:'global'} for every conversation; this matches the current API (no per-user resource scoping, RBAC is post-v0.5) and the project-scope path is exercised only by tests/integration/ai/tools.test.ts.; Non-blocking: abortableBackend (ask-service.ts) stops waiting on abort but does not forward the ask signal into queryServiceLogs/log-sources.ts, so an in-flight SSH docker.logs_window read runs on until runtimeTimeoutMs (15s default) after a client disconnect; bounded, but not a true cancel.; Non-blocking: the ask path uses provider.toolCall (non-streaming) and emits the final answer as post-hoc 200-char text chunks; provider.stream is implemented and contract-tested but unused, so time-to-first-token equals a full model turn.; Non-blocking: askQuestion consumes a rate-limit slot before checking that a provider is configured, so AI_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED replies count against the per-user window.; Non-blocking: the Anthropic wire shape (thinking adaptive, output_config.effort, strict tools, tool_choice auto) is validated only against MSW fixtures per ADR 0012; real-API verification remains opt-in/nightly as the ai-readonly skill prescribes.; Hardening expectation 'slow KDF' is inapplicable to the BYOK key (it must be recoverable to call the provider); it is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted in credentials via encryptSecret with key versioning, and no new user passwords are introduced by this phase.
